_meta.title: Chintan Turakhia — Coinbase × Linear
_meta.why_strong: Sharp executive worldview with quotable lines ('I don't think developers are slow, I think companies are slow'), precise trigger tied to external change (AI agents becoming 'genuinely capable' in early 2026), metric-anchored pain (merged PRs/day), and explicit decision context (top-down mandate — he ordered engineers to delete IDEs for 2 weeks).

persona.name: Champion Chintan, Head of Engineering, AI-acceleration mandate
persona.location_context: San Francisco, runs Base App engineering org at Coinbase, on-the-ground responsibility for shipping
persona.primary_job: When my engineers are spending 30% of their day answering Slack questions instead of merging PRs, and AI agents have just become genuinely capable, I want to give the agents structured queryable knowledge so they can do the coordination work, so I can stop being slower than my hiring promised we would be.

pain_points.label: Knowledge scattered across heads + Slack + meetings
pain_points.description: Critical context lives in Slack threads from 6 weeks ago, in PMs' heads, in unrecorded standup decisions; agents (and new hires) can't find any of it

pain_points.label: Hidden tax of context-switching
pain_points.description: Engineers interrupted constantly to answer 'what was the decision on X' — measurable drag on merged-PRs-per-day metric

pain_points.label: Coordination overhead bottlenecking shipping
pain_points.description: By early 2026 AI agents are capable enough to ship code; the limit is org coordination, not engineer skill

trust_needs: Used by other engineering orgs at peer companies (Ramp, Vercel-tier)
API + webhook surface deep enough that agents can query reliably
Doesn't require migration from existing toolchain (Linear specifically: not a rip-and-replace)
decision_triggers: Personal demo where his team's actual workflow is the example
Existing usage signal from his team (someone already adopted it bottom-up)
Clear path to having agents read/write tickets autonomously
objections: What about Jira migration cost / muscle memory of existing engineers?
Is the data model open enough that we can build our own integrations?
Will this be slow at our scale?
persona.channel_behavior: X / LinkedIn for industry signal; podcasts on commute; reads founder posts; ignores cold outbound entirely

verbatim_quotes: I don't think developers are slow, I think companies are slow.
I'm not designing things for humans anymore. I'm designing things for agents.
Why can't an agent do this, and how do we make it possible?
